ordinance: Ballot Measure 2 (2020), section 24, which added AS 15.15.350(c) to (g), adopted by the voters on 2020-11-03 (valid_from is the date of the vote, not of its certification, which came later; no Alaska table is dated between the two, so the join is the same either way); 6 AAC 25.071 and 6 AAC 25.072, effective 2022-02-24 (Register 241, April 2022, by their history notes as Cornell LII prints them), so these two cells did not exist before that date and no Alaska table falls before it; AS 15.40.220 as amended by section 49 of the same measure, for the special election of 2022-08-16; AS 15.15.360(d)(3), AS 15.15.365, AS 15.15.460 and AS 15.20.430 to 15.20.530 are cited without a date, which no saved source gives
evidence: overvote: AS 15.15.350(e)(1); skipped and max_consecutive_skips: AS 15.15.350(e)(2) and (g)(6); duplicate: 6 AAC 25.072 with AS 15.15.350(g)(6); batch_elimination: 6 AAC 25.071 with AS 15.15.365; threshold and one_seat_stop: AS 15.15.350(d), (d)(1) and (d)(2); surplus_transfer, surplus_decimals and last_defeat_transfer: AS 15.15.350(d) and (d)(1); inactive ballots: AS 15.15.350(f) and (g)(2); a write-in mark in a race where no write-in candidate filed: AS 15.15.360(d)(3); ties, which have no column: AS 15.15.350(e)(3), AS 15.15.460 and AS 15.20.430 to 15.20.530; the special election: AS 15.40.220. duplicate: no text says whether a ranking 6 AAC 25.072 disregards is a blank one; it is read as one, a skipped ranking under (g)(6), the reading the Division's 2022 RCV Detailed Reports follow. batch_elimination: the write-in rankings are then left out of round 1, as the Division's 2022 General Election Media Packet says ('rankings for them will be excluded') and its RCV Detailed Reports show. threshold and one_seat_stop: the majority test is made on the initial tabulation with the write-ins pooled, before 6 AAC 25.071, and again in round 1 after a 6 AAC 25.071 defeat. surplus_transfer, surplus_decimals and last_defeat_transfer are na: one vote per ballot, and the count ends at two continuing candidates. A write-in mark in a race where no write-in candidate filed: the first on a ballot counts for nobody and is passed over, not a skipped ranking, by AS 15.15.360(d)(3) and the Division's setting 'Exclude unresolved write-ins' ('a ranking for a write-in will not be considered a blank or skipped ranking'); a later one is a duplicate ranking, as below. A second or later write-in mark on a ballot is a duplicate ranking too, read as duplicate says. That rests on no statute or regulation but on the Division's own cast vote records, which flag every such mark DuplicatedRcvCandidate as they flag a candidate ranked twice (1,632 marks in the records of the 2022 special and general elections, and none of the 60,508 first write-in marks), and on its count, which follows the flag: it changes 3 ballots, the whole difference between a recount of the special and U.S. Senate tables and the Division's reports. The Division's 2022 General Election Media Packet reads the other way ('a ranking for a write-in will not be considered a blank or skipped ranking').

ordinance: Constitution Act 1902, Seventh Schedule (Sch 7), inserted by the Constitution (Amendment) Act 1979 No 38, assented to 1979-04-30, and not amended since by its history note in the versions in force on the three poll dates (effective 2014-10-28, 2018-07-01 and 2022-11-28); for the marking and formality of a ballot paper, the Parliamentary Electorates and Elections Act 1912 (1912 Act; the version of 2014-12-01) for 2015, and the Electoral Act 2017 (2017 Act; assented to 2017-11-30, commenced 2018-07-01, which repealed the 1912 Act) for 2019 and 2023
evidence: overvote: Sch 7 cl 2(3)(a), with 1912 Act s 122A(2)(a) and 2017 Act s 165(3)(b)(i); skipped and max_consecutive_skips: Sch 7 cl 2(3)(b), with 1912 Act s 122A(2)(b) and 2017 Act s 165(3)(b)(ii); duplicate: 1912 Act s 103(2) and Sch 4, 2017 Act s 132(2) and Sch 4; batch_elimination: Sch 7 cl 7(1) and 8(1); threshold: Sch 7 cl 2(2), 4, 5, 7(2) and 8(1); surplus_transfer and surplus_decimals: Sch 7 cl 5, 7(2) and 8(2), which elect one candidate, with no clause on a surplus; last_defeat_transfer: Sch 7 cl 9; one_seat_stop: Sch 7 cl 9 and 10(1); ties, which have no column: Sch 7 cl 10; formality, which has no column: 1912 Act ss 122 and 122A, 2017 Act s 165. One rule set: the count is Sch 7, which each of the Commission's 279 preferences pages of 2015, 2019 and 2023 names ("The legislation defining the LA count can be found at Constitution Act - Seventh Schedule"). Sch 7 has the same words in the versions in force on 2015-03-28, 2019-03-23 and 2023-03-25 (three colons are dashes in the last), and each carries only the note of its insertion ("Seventh Sch: Ins 1979 No 38, Sch 1 (6)."). valid_from is the assent of that Act ("Constitution (Amendment) Act 1979 No 38 Assented to 30.04.1979."), the earliest adoption among the texts that made the rule set: every cell but duplicate rests on Sch 7, and duplicate rests on the marking provisions of the two Acts, whose dates in ordinance are later (2014-12-01 and 2017-11-30). The Electoral Acts settle only the marking and the formality of a paper, and no cell changes between them: after a single 1, a repeated preference or a break in the order leaves the paper formal under both (1912 Act s 122A(2), 2017 Act s 165(3)(b)), and the 2017 Act adds that the later preferences are treated as if not recorded, which Sch 7 cl 2(3) already says at all three dates. The 1912 Act of 2014-12-01 is read in AustLII's consolidation ("As at 1 December 2014") and in the government's version of 2013-07-01, which give each quoted provision in the same words. duplicate is na: the voter writes "the number “1” in the square opposite the name of the candidate" (1912 Act s 103(2), 2017 Act s 132(2)), the form in Sch 4 of each Act says "Write the number 1 in the square next to the candidate of your choice.", and among the 33,747,873 rows of the Commission's 279 preference files no paper names a candidate twice. threshold: "a majority of the first preference votes" elects on the first count (cl 5), counted on "all ballot-papers not rejected by him as informal" (cl 4), and "a majority of the votes remaining in the count" on every later count (cl 7(2), 8(1)), that is more than one-half of the papers not exhausted (cl 2(2), "a ballot-paper on which there is not recorded a vote for a continuing candidate"). The Commission prints this absolute majority at every count of all 279 distributions, floor(T/2)+1 of the T votes in the count, and its distributions go on past the count at which the winner has it until two candidates remain ("for statistical purposes a DoP will still be conducted such that only two candidates remain in the count"); the candidate elected does not change. last_defeat_transfer and one_seat_stop: the one continuing candidate left is elected without a transfer ("shall not be repeated where there is only 1 continuing candidate, but that 1 continuing candidate shall be elected."), which with two continuing candidates happens only after the two tie (cl 10(1), "those candidates being the only continuing candidates"). Ties: cl 10(1)(a) excludes the tied candidate who "had the fewest number of votes at the last count at which they did not have an equal number of votes", and otherwise cl 10(1)(b) and 10(2) one whose slip is "drawn at random". The one tie for exclusion in the 279 tables is rcv_nsw_20190323_la_newcastle at count 1, c06 and c08 on 854 each, with no earlier count; the page excludes c06 and prints no draw. Formality: the tables carry the Commission's ruling in cov_formality. Both Acts read a lone tick or cross as the 1 (1912 Act s 122A(4), 2017 Act s 165(3)(d)) and disregard crosses beside a 1 or a tick ("treated as if the marks in those other squares did not appear", s 122A(5), s 165(3)(e)), in the same words. Three patterns beside a single 1, one cross and nothing else, other numbers and crosses, and a tick, were Formal in 2015 (342, 458 and 564 papers), as the Commission's 2015 data entry rules read them ("shall be treated as if the ticks and/or crosses did not appear on the ballot paper"), and Informal in 2019 (535, 598 and 777) and in 2023 (334, 599 and 769). valid_to is empty: the legislative history captured on 2026-01-17 still notes Sch 7 only as "Seventh Sch Ins 1979 No 38, Sch 1 (6).", and the one later amendment of a cited provision of the 2017 Act is 2022 No 57, Sch 2 ("Sec 165 Am 2022 No 57, Sch 2[15]." and "Sch 4 Am 2022 No 57, Sch 2[16]."), which commenced after the 2023 poll ("Date of commencement of Sch 2, 1.10.2024, sec 2(2)."). It adds a logo beside a name on the form ("Insert the candidate’s logo or the registered party logo") and, in s 165(3)(h), a saving for a paper written by hand that lacks it ("by reason of the failure of the ballot paper having printed on it"); it changes no cell.

ordinance: New York City Charter section 1057-g, added by a vote of the electors on 2019-11-05 (Question 1 of the 2019 Charter Revision Commission) and applying to elections held on or after 2021-01-01 (subdivision j). Subdivisions a, b, c, e, f and g to k have the same words in the captures of 2021-01-27, 2022-10-15 and 2025-06-03; the two amendments its history line names, Local Law 3 of 2023 and 2023 N.Y. Laws ch. 481, change subdivision d, the ballot design, only
sections: Charter 1057-g(a); Charter 1057-g(b); Charter 1057-g(d)(1); Charter 1057-g(e)(1); Charter 1057-g(e)(2); Charter 1057-g(e)(2)(a); Charter 1057-g(e)(2)(b); Charter 1057-g(e)(3); Charter 1057-g(f)(2); Charter 1057-g(j); Charter 25(b)(7)
evidence: overvote: Charter 1057-g(a), exhausted ballot; skipped and max_consecutive_skips: 1057-g(a), highest rank, and 1057-g(e)(2), with the 2019 Commission's report, since no section names a limit; duplicate: the Commission's report and the Board's manual, since no section speaks of it; batch_elimination: 1057-g(a), batch elimination and election is mathematically impossible, and 1057-g(e)(2)(b), with the write-in line's own round from the Board's records; threshold: 1057-g(e)(1) and (e)(2); one_seat_stop and last_defeat_transfer: 1057-g(e)(2)(a); surplus_transfer and surplus_decimals: one seat, 1057-g(a), ranked choice voting; ties, which have no column: 1057-g(e)(3). valid_from is the vote (Local Law 3 of 2023: "as added by a vote of the electors on November 5, 2019"); the code's own history line reads "L.L. 2019/215, 12/11/2019, eff. 12/11/2019", and no table depends on the choice. Primaries and the two 2025 special elections are one rule set: 1057-g(a) covers "any primary election for a ranked choice office, and any election for a ranked choice office in which all candidates are nominated by independent nominating petition", and 25(b)(7) makes a council vacancy such an election. overvote: "a ballot that assigns equal rank to two or more candidates and all candidates with higher ranks than the rank assigned to two or more candidates are eliminated" is exhausted, and the Commission says "Ballots that assign the same rank to more than one candidate would not count when that rank is reached." skipped: each ballot counts for "its highest ranked continuing candidate", and the Commission says "those skipped ranks would be ignored". duplicate: the Commission says it "would simply count in the same way it would have if only the highest of those ranks was marked", and the Board's manual that "Marking the same candidate for more than one choice is not an over-voted ballot." batch_elimination: a candidate goes whose total, with what could transfer from candidates with fewer or equal votes, "would not be enough to surpass that of the candidate with the next highest vote total", and no such batch runs where it "would result in only one continuing candidate". The Board's footnote states the test as a total "less than the votes for the candidate immediately ahead of them", which keeps a group equal to the next total; no published round tells the two apart. Where the largest group would leave one candidate the next largest goes, as the Board's rounds show in 3 tables. The write-in line going alone at the end of round 1 rests on no section but on the Board's records: the manual has "all the write-in candidates will be eliminated as a group in the next round", and all 59 contests that go past round 1 show it. Its votes do not count in that round's batch test, since the test does not run there. threshold: "If a candidate receives a majority of highest rank votes" elects before any elimination, and the Board's footnote says "over 50% of the vote in round 1"; its round 1 percentages in all 124 HTML pages are votes over the listed rows, write-ins included, so that is the base here. After round 1 no text tests a majority, and "If there are two continuing candidates, the candidate with the most votes shall be declared the nominee". Ties: "A tie between two or more candidates shall be resolved in accordance with the election law."; none of the 127 tables reaches one.

ordinance: City Charter section 1105, Measure O, voted on 2006-11-07, in the text the Council put on the ballot on 2006-07-18; the current text could not be read, and no amendment was found
sections: Charter 1105(C); Charter 1105(D); Charter 1105(E); Charter 1105(F); Charter 1105(G); Charter 1105(H)
evidence: overvote: Charter 1105(H); skipped and max_consecutive_skips: 1105(G); duplicate: 1105(D) and the county's rounds; batch_elimination: 1105(D) and the county's rounds, against 1105(F); threshold: 1105(D); last_defeat_transfer: 1105(D), the same sentence as duplicate, which has no exception for the last elimination, so a final defeat on an exact tie of two moves those votes; one_seat_stop: 1105(D); ties, which have no column: 1105(E). overvote: "shall not count towards any candidate in that round or in subsequent rounds." skipped: "In the first or any round, in the event that any ballot reaches a ranking with no candidate indicated", and the county's pages show any number of skips passed over. duplicate: "every ballot counting towards that candidate shall be advanced to the next-ranked continuing candidate." threshold: "After every round, if any candidate receives a majority of votes from the continuing ballots, that candidate shall be declared the winner." batch_elimination: 1105(F) has "eliminated simultaneously, and those ballots advanced to the next-ranked continuing", while the rounds have "the candidate receiving the smallest number of votes shall be eliminated". Every county page and report eliminates one candidate per round, also where the text would take several at once, so batch_elimination follows them. Write-ins: the county's pages of 2010 print a Write-In row with the votes the table gives the pooled line; from 2012 the row is zero or gone and a write-in mark is passed over, so `writein_filed` carries it table by table. The date is the vote, "the voters of the City of Oakland approved Measure". The 2022 reports were run with a setting that held a ballot with no valid first choice out of round 1; the county says it "should have been configured to advance ballots to the next ranking immediately when no candidate was selected for a particular round." Counted so, the 6 tables not re-tabulated equal those reports in every figure.

ordinance: City Charter article III section 5 paragraph 12, Measure I, on the ballot of 2004-03-02, which only let the Council establish instant runoff voting by ordinance, and Municipal Code chapter 2.14, whose section texts and date could not be read; the county's rounds and the city's candidate handbook carry the cells
evidence: All cells rest on the county's rounds and the city's handbook, since only the headings of Municipal Code 2.14 could be read. overvote: the handbook; skipped and max_consecutive_skips: the county's page note; duplicate: the handbook; batch_elimination: the handbook and the county's rounds; threshold and one_seat_stop: the handbook; ties, which have no column: Municipal Code 2.14.050, its heading only. overvote: "No. If a voter gives more than one candidate the same ranking, the vote cannot be counted. Only one candidate can represent the voter's choice in each column." skipped: "NOTE: The Ranked-Choice Voting Report for Round 1 combines the accumulated totals of first-choice rankings as well as the second- or third-choice selections transferred to the first-choice ranking selections when the first-choice ranking was skipped." duplicate: "If a voter ranks one candidate as the voter's first, second and third choice, it is the same as if the voter leaves the second or third choice blank." batch_elimination: "The candidate who received the fewest first-choice votes is eliminated." threshold: "Election to the office of Auditor and City Council requires a 50% + 1 majority vote threshold." one_seat_stop: "This elimination process will continue until one candidate receives a majority and is deemed the winner." Every county page and report eliminates one candidate per round, also where the text would take several at once, so batch_elimination follows them. Write-ins: the county's pages of 2010 print a Write-In row with the votes the table gives the pooled line; from 2012 the row is zero or gone and a write-in mark is passed over, so `writein_filed` carries it table by table. "Only qualified Write-In candidates can receive votes." The handbook is the edition for 2026, carried back on the county's rounds to 2010. valid_from is not an adoption of the counting text: it is the ballot date of Measure I, from a League of Women Voters flyer, which reports no result, and the Charter of 2020 holds the paragraph. No table before 2010-11-02 depends on it. last_defeat_transfer is na: with a majority tested at every count, a final defeat comes only on an exact tie of two, and no text saved speaks of it.

ordinance: 21-A M.R.S. section 723-A, enacted by Initiated Bill 2015, c. 3, adopted by the voters on 2016-11-08 and applying to elections on or after 2018-01-01, as amended by PL 2017, c. 316 and PL 2019, c. 320, which change no cell here; with 29-250 C.M.R. ch. 535, the emergency rule effective 2018-05-11 and the rule effective 2018-11-07
evidence: batch_elimination: 723-A(1)(A), (1)(G) and (4)(B) ("Two or more candidates may be defeated simultaneously by batch elimination in any round of tabulation."), the write-in line among them; last_defeat_transfer: 723-A(2)(A), "2 or fewer". The text says "would not be enough to surpass"; no group in these tables equals the next total. On 2018-11-06 no ch. 535 was in force by the Secretary's filing in federal court ("they expired in 90 days"; "eff. Nov. 7, 2018"), so that count's duplicate rests on the Secretary's own report, which the row reproduces. overvote: 723-A(1)(D) and ch. 535 s 4(2)(B)(1); skipped and max_consecutive_skips: 723-A(1)(D), (1)(K) and ch. 535 s 4(2)(B)(2) and (3); duplicate: ch. 535 s 4(2)(B)(4), since the statute has no sentence on it; threshold: ch. 535 s 4(2)(A); one_seat_stop: 723-A(2)(A); surplus_transfer and surplus_decimals: one seat; ties, which have no column: 723-A(3); write-ins: 696(2)(E), with the Secretary of State's Summary Reports. overvote: an exhausted ballot "contains an overvote at the highest continuing ranking or contains 2 or more sequential skipped rankings before its highest continuing ranking". duplicate: "the vote for the next continuing candidate ranked by that voter will be counted in the next round". threshold: "If no candidate receives more than 50% of the first choice votes based on the election returns provided by municipalities" the rounds run, and 723-A itself has no majority sentence until 2025, only "If there are 2 or fewer continuing candidates, the candidate with the most votes is declared the winner of the election."; no contest here tells a majority of active ballots from one of all ballots in round 1. write-ins: a mark for a person "who has not filed a declaration of write-in candidacy" is not counted ("the vote for that office may not be counted", and the Secretary's FAQ: "will not be tallied and will be recorded as blanks"); the Summary Reports count it for nobody and go on to the next ranking, not reading it as a skip: the 2024 report equals the table so read, and differs by 22 ballots if the mark is a blank. Whether a candidate declared is in counting_values.csv, from whether the report prints a Write-in row. The saved sources print no list of declared candidates.

ordinance: 21-A M.R.S. section 723-A as amended by PL 2023, c. 304, Part A, an emergency law that took effect on approval, 2023-06-26, and PL 2023, c. 628; with 29-250 C.M.R. ch. 535, the rule effective 2018-11-07
evidence: batch_elimination: PL 2023, c. 304 repeals 723-A(1)(A), (1)(G) and (4)(B) ("A. [PL 2023, c. 304, Pt. A, §14 (RP).]", "G. [PL 2023, c. 304, Pt. A, §15 (RP).]", "B. [PL 2023, c. 304, Pt. A, §16 (RP).]"), while ch. 535 in its capture of 2024-11-16 still says "More than one candidate may be defeated in a single round by batch elimination"; the statute governs here, and the one table, whose count has two candidates, tests neither. valid_from is the day the emergency law took effect on approval, "Effective June 26, 2023, unless otherwise indicated."; no table depends on it. overvote: 723-A(1)(D) and ch. 535 s 4(2)(B)(1); skipped and max_consecutive_skips: 723-A(1)(D), (1)(K) and ch. 535 s 4(2)(B)(2) and (3); duplicate: ch. 535 s 4(2)(B)(4), since the statute has no sentence on it; threshold: ch. 535 s 4(2)(A); one_seat_stop: 723-A(2)(A); surplus_transfer and surplus_decimals: one seat; ties, which have no column: 723-A(3); write-ins: 696(2)(E), with the Secretary of State's Summary Reports. overvote: an exhausted ballot "contains an overvote at the highest continuing ranking or contains 2 or more sequential skipped rankings before its highest continuing ranking". duplicate: "the vote for the next continuing candidate ranked by that voter will be counted in the next round". threshold: "If no candidate receives more than 50% of the first choice votes based on the election returns provided by municipalities" the rounds run, and 723-A itself has no majority sentence until 2025, only "If there are 2 or fewer continuing candidates, the candidate with the most votes is declared the winner of the election."; no contest here tells a majority of active ballots from one of all ballots in round 1. write-ins: a mark for a person "who has not filed a declaration of write-in candidacy" is not counted ("the vote for that office may not be counted", and the Secretary's FAQ: "will not be tallied and will be recorded as blanks"); the Summary Reports count it for nobody and go on to the next ranking, not reading it as a skip: the 2024 report equals the table so read, and differs by 22 ballots if the mark is a blank. Whether a candidate declared is in counting_values.csv, from whether the report prints a Write-in row. The saved sources print no list of declared candidates.

ordinance: City and County Charter section 13.102, Proposition A, voted on 2002-03-05, with no amendment recorded; the Department's reports show how it was counted
evidence: overvote, skipped and max_consecutive_skips: Charter 13.102; duplicate: the State's staff report of 2006 and the 2008 requirements table, and the Department's rounds; ties, which have no column: Charter 13.102. overvote: "If a ranked-choice ballot gives equal rank to two or more candidates, the ballot shall be declared exhausted when such multiple rankings are reached." skipped: "If a voter casts a ranked-choice ballot but skips a rank, the voter's vote shall be transferred to that voter's next ranked choice." duplicate: "the later choice for the candidate is seen by the system as an under-vote." "multiple votes for a single candidate count only once." batch_elimination: Charter 13.102(e) and the pages; threshold, last_defeat_transfer and one_seat_stop: Charter 13.102. The Charter's text is the same for all three rule sets; where it and the Department's pages differ, the row follows the pages. batch_elimination: "If the total number of votes of the two or more candidates credited with the lowest number of votes is less than the number of votes credited to the candidate with the next highest number of votes, those candidates with the lowest number of votes shall be eliminated simultaneously and their votes transferred to the next-ranked continuing candidate on each ballot in a single counting operation.", which the pages of 2004 to 2006 run from the lowest up, stopping at the first candidate the total reaches; the rounds of 2004 District 1 and 2006 District 6 fail any larger group. threshold: "If, after this transfer of votes, any candidate has a majority of the votes from the continuing ballots, that candidate shall be declared elected." one_seat_stop: "This process of eliminating candidates and transferring their votes to the next-ranked continuing candidates shall be repeated until a candidate receives a majority of the votes from the continuing ballots." last_defeat_transfer: "All votes cast for that candidate shall be transferred to the next-ranked continuing candidate on each voter's ballot." Write-ins: the Department's reports count the pooled write-in line in the tables of 2006 to 2010, so writein_filed carries it table by table; the saved sources print no list of declared candidates. valid_from is the vote, "Passed 55% - 45% on March 5, 2002". valid_to is the first election on the Sequoia system, not an adoption. First use was 2004-11-02; no saved text moves the Charter's date for it.
